summary: Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) specialized in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. His career included posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Toyo Bunko, and presidency at Reitaku University.

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate under Hakuju Ui at the University of Tokyo, where he was professor from 1954 to 1973, and later directed the Eastern Institute.

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) focused on Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University, and CASS under Xianlin Ji. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.

Hajime Sakurabe (1925–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, earning a PhD. He held posts at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and was professor at Otani University.

Hajime Tanabe (1885–1962) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, as well as in Germany under Heidegger, Rickert, and Husserl. Influenced by Kitaro Nishida, he taught at Kyoto University from 1919 to 1945.
Hakuin Ekaku (1686–1769) was active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Dōkyō Etan around 1708 and under Hakuyūshi around 1710–1711, and he taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui (1882–1963) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo, as well as at Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He taught at Tohoku University, Tokyo, and Komazawa University.

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani (1885–1973) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Toshima Normal School and trained under several masters, notably Sogaku Harada from 1925 to 1943, and founded Sanbo Zen in 1954.

Hakuyu Hadano (1916–1989) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served on the faculty at Tohoku University, where he was an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later professor emeritus.

Halle O'Neal works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler (attested 2011) and holds a co-director post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Hammalawa Saddhatissa (1914–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sastrodaya and Vidyodaya Pirivenas, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Edinburgh. He taught at BHU and Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990).
Hank Glassman is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He has held a faculty post at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

Hanna Havnevik works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Oslo, serving as professor (attested 2006–2008) and later as professor emerita (attested 2026).

Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate under William Dwight Whitney at Yale University, where he taught until 1917, and later held chairs at the University of Marburg and the University of Munich.

Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and served as professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from 1965 to 2000.

Hans Delbrück (1848–1929) was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held academic posts at Frederick William University Berlin in 1885 and at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1921.

Hans Harder (born 1966) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das in 1997. He worked at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and joined Heidelberg University in 2007.

Hans Hartog (born 1912) was an Indologist. He studied at Tübingen, Bethel, Munich, and the University of Marburg, earning his PhD (1937–1939) under Friedrich Heiler and studying under scholars including Walther Wüst and Hanns Oertel.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder (1896–1957) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock (born 1938) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed graduate studies at Northwestern and Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill, and served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967).
